topics.topic: Precision and normalization of inbound non-allocation monetary values
questions: For monetary input with more than two fractional digits, must the boundary reject it, or quantize it with `ROUND_HALF_UP`; and does allocation-sum validation occur before or after that normalization?
At each monetary input boundary, what happens to finite Decimal values with fewer or more than two fractional digits?
For non-allocation monetary inputs with excess fractional precision, must the boundary reject them, round them half-up, or accept them until storage?

quotes:
The amount quantized to two digits, ROUND_HALF_UP. An amount with more
fraction digits is rounded, never refused, and the sign rule is applied to
the rounded amount.

`capability:expense_intake.create_expense_from_recognition` accepts only a
   confirmed complete result of a supported contract version, validates the
   total (`capability:financial_policy.validate_eur_amount`) and the explicit
   allocations — shape, exact sum, no proportional split, then every section
   of the project, read through `module:portal_store`'s section repository in
   a read-only transaction it closes first — then in one transaction looks up the
   `recognized_document_id`: absent — insert the expense, its allocations and
   one client-visible document and append `expense.create`; same fingerprint —
   return the existing expense as replay; different — conflict.
judgement.why: State 5 says non-allocation monetary inputs are rounded half-up to two digits rather than refused and places total normalization before the allocation shape and exact-sum checks.

topics.topic: Precision and observable rounding of overall progress results
questions: How is overall_progress_percent represented and rounded when the weighted division has no finite Decimal result?
To how many fractional digits is overall_progress_percent rounded, and is that quantization part of the observable result?

quotes:
The weighted R9 progress over sections with positive planned work and a
reported percent, rounded to two fraction digits as money is (A9), or `None`
when that denominator is zero.
judgement.why: State 5 fixes the observable overall-progress result at two fractional digits.

topics.topic: Precision, normalization, and sum-check timing for allocations
questions: May an allocation with more than two fractional digits be accepted and stored when the allocation list sums exactly to the expense total, or must each allocation independently satisfy the 2-digit money rule?
May an allocation with more than two fraction digits be accepted and stored, or must it be rejected or quantized to two digits before the allocation-sum check?

quotes:
The former `amount (> 0)` is not a rule of the accepted spec 459ac96c or its
code (`core/models.py` `AllocationInstruction`: unbounded `Decimal`;
`domain/expense_management.py` `_validate_allocation_sum` and
`application/expense_intake.py` `_validate_initial_allocations` check only
the sum and, on correction and re-allocation, a non-empty list).

- **Fields:** `allocation_id: UUID`, `expense_id: UUID`,
  `target: AllocationTargetKind (section | other_expenses)`,
  `section_id: UUID | None` `[closed-choice: required iff target =
  section]`, `amount: Decimal` (as instructed, M26), `created_at`, `created_by`,
  `updated_at | None`, `updated_by | None`.

- `Decimal`, 2 fraction digits, `ROUND_HALF_UP` at derivation boundaries;
  stored amounts are already 2-digit exact.
judgement.divergence: One passage accepts an unbounded allocation Decimal and stores it as instructed, while the other forbids any stored monetary amount that is not already exact to two fractional digits; the operator and later readers observe exact high-precision values versus their absence or normalization.
judgement.why: The new allocation passages expressly permit storage as instructed without a precision check, contradicting State 2's invariant that stored amounts are two-digit exact.

bases.rests_on:
- Money is `Decimal` with 2 fraction digits, currency always `EUR`; rounding
  policy is a State 2 rule. Negative amounts never appear in stored records,
  with one named exception: an expense allocation amount (M26, M29);
  otherwise negative values exist only in derived values: balances, and
  the sums over such allocations (never clamped).

witness.initial: An active project has a valid EUR expense whose total is 10.00 and an authorized operator may replace its allocations.
events: The operator submits allocations of 0.001 and 9.999, whose exact sum is 10.00.
outcomes: M26 and M29 permit the exact unbounded Decimal values to be accepted and stored as instructed.
A9 does not permit those exact values to be stored because stored amounts must already be two-digit exact.
witness.observer: The operator and subsequent expense readers
basis:
For an active project an operator can: correct, include, or exclude an
expense; allocate or manually split it across sections or `Other expenses`
(allocation sum equals the expense total; automatic proportional split is
forbidden); update manual work progress per section (0–100%); register work
payments (idempotent by stable payment identity); publish progress photos and
manage caption, section association, and visibility; maintain the manual
budget; review and activate imported budget versions.

An expense's instruction list must be non-empty and sum to the expense
  total (at creation the total is positive, so an empty list never sums);
  an individual amount's sign is not constrained (zero and negative
  amounts are accepted and stored, M29).

questions: Must a foreign-currency expense expose a typed `currency_mismatch`, or use the generic empty HTTP 422 response required by A7?

quotes:
Every refusal before the replay check answers
HTTP 422 with an empty body (`rules.http_router_backend.error_policy`), so
which of them failed first is not observable to the caller; a replay with
other content is the conflict of A8 (409).
judgement.why: A7 specifically defines the public response for the expense currency check; the typed currency classification does not alter that empty HTTP 422 response.

judgement.divergence: With accepted higher-precision allocations, one implementation rounds each section before summing displayed components, while another aggregates exact allocations and rounds only each final total; staff and viewers see totals that respectively do or do not equal the displayed rounded section values.
judgement.why: The texts require rounding at derivation boundaries but never identify whether section actuals or aggregate totals are the relevant boundary or require reconciliation with displayed components.

topics.topic: Rounding order used to calculate overall progress
questions: Must overall progress be calculated directly from unrounded weighted products, or from the rounded per-section completed-work values?

quotes:
- Completed work value: `work_planned × completion_percent / 100`, rounded
  half-up to 2 digits per section, summed after rounding.

- Overall progress: `Σ(work_planned × percent) / Σ(work_planned)` over
  sections of the active version with `work_planned > 0` and a recorded
  progress (a section without a progress record is left out of both sums);
  undefined (shown unavailable) when the denominator is 0.
judgement.why: A9 defines overall progress directly from the weighted products, independently of the separately rounded completed-work values.

topics.topic: Whether an existing expense may be corrected to zero
questions: May an existing expense be corrected to `total_amount = 0.00` with a non-empty allocation set summing to zero, or must every corrected total remain strictly positive?

judgement.why: P1 asks and answers the same question on the same changed allocation and correction passages.

precedent.topic: Whether an expense amount correction may set total_amount to zero
quotes:
A9 (the total in EUR, non-negative), A19 (every section target of this
project, exact sum), A24, A13 (`expense.correct`); no intermediate state
commits. The allocation list must hold at least one instruction whatever
the total; an empty list is refused, a zero total included. An individual
amount is not otherwise checked (State 1 M26), so a zero total is corrected
with, for example, one zero allocation.
precedent.why: State 5 explicitly permits correcting an expense to a zero total with a non-empty allocation list summing to zero.
